On Windows, we use the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2) to run
Fastmixture, ADAMIXTURE and Clumppling inside Ubuntu. R and RStudio stay
on Windows, and `tidygenclust` handles the connection to Linux
automatically. We do not need to install R or RStudio inside Ubuntu.

Windows support is experimental and currently requires an Intel/AMD
x86-64 computer, Windows 11 (or Windows 10 with WSL2 support), internet
access and several GB of free disk space. Windows on ARM is not
supported.

# Set up WSL2 and Ubuntu

Microsoft's [WSL setup
guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/setup/environment)
explains how to get started with Ubuntu. If Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 is
already installed with WSL2, we can reuse it and skip the installation
command. Otherwise, open **PowerShell as Administrator** from the Start
menu and run:

``` powershell
wsl --install -d Ubuntu-24.04
```

Restart Windows if requested, then open **Ubuntu 24.04** from the Start
menu and create a Linux username and password. The password is not
displayed as we type it.

In **PowerShell**, check the distribution name and version:

``` powershell
wsl --list --verbose
```

The `VERSION` column should show `2`. If it shows `1`, run
`wsl --set-version Ubuntu-24.04 2`, replacing the name if needed.

In the **Ubuntu terminal**, install the tools needed to build and
download the analysis packages. First, please run:

``` bash
sudo apt update
```
When it finishes, continue with:

``` bash
sudo apt install -y build-essential curl git ca-certificates tar gzip
```

We can now close Ubuntu; `tidygenclust` starts it when needed.

# Install tidygenclust

In **Windows RStudio**, install the development version from the
`windows` branch on GitHub, which contains the experimental Windows
support:

```{r install_package, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("EvolEcolGroup/tidygenclust@windows")
```

If working from a local development copy, open its RStudio project and
use `devtools::load_all()` instead of the GitHub installation and
`library(tidygenclust)` below. If R asks for build tools, install the
[Rtools version matching
R](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/).

To select our Ubuntu distribution, open the Windows R `.Renviron` file:

```{r select_distribution, eval=FALSE}
file.edit(path.expand("~/.Renviron"))
```

Add this line, using the name from `wsl --list --verbose` and keeping
any existing settings:

``` text
TIDYGENCLUST_WSL_DISTRO=Ubuntu-24.04
```

Save with a final newline, then select **Session \> Restart R**. If the
distribution is named simply `Ubuntu`, this setting is not needed.

# Install the analysis tools

In **Windows RStudio**, run:

```{r install_tools, eval=FALSE}
library(tidygenclust)
tgc_tools_install(adamixture = TRUE)
tgc_tools_version()
```

The first installation takes several minutes. The package installs
Python and the required environments inside Ubuntu; no Windows Python
installation is needed. ADAMIXTURE is optional: omit `adamixture = TRUE`
if it is not needed, in which case its reported version may be `NA`.
Repeating the installer reuses existing environments and checks the
requested tool revisions.

We can now follow the [main vignette](tidygenclust.html) in Windows
RStudio, using ordinary Windows paths on a local drive. The analysis
functions use WSL automatically, and their results work with the usual
plotting methods. Classic ADMIXTURE, provided by
`tidypopgen::gt_admixture()`, is not included in this Windows support.

If setup fails, check the Ubuntu name and the first error in the
installation log. When reporting a problem, include `sessionInfo()`,
`tgc_tools_version()` and the output of `wsl --list --verbose`.
